TRIPLE LINKING NUMBERS, AMBIGUOUS HOPF INVARIANTS
AND INTEGRAL FORMULAS FOR THREE-COMPONENT LINKS
DENNIS DETURCK, HERMAN GLUCK, RAFAL KOMENDARCZYK,
PAUL MELVIN, CLAYTON SHONKWILER, AND DAVID SHEA VELA-VICK
To Manfredo do Carmo
in friendship and admiration, on his 80th birthday
Abstract. Three-component links in the 3-dimensional sphere were classiﬁed up to
link homotopy by John Milnor in his senior thesis, published in 1954. A complete set

blocks.title: Statement of results
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:results label="sec:results"}

Consider the configuration space $$\mathrm{Conf}_3S^3\subset S^3 \times S^3 \times S^3$$ of ordered triples $(x,y,z)$ of distinct points in the unit $3$-sphere $S^3$ in $\mathbb R^4$. Since $x$, $y$ and $z$ are distinct, they span a $2$-plane in $\mathbb R^4$. Orient this plane so that the vectors from $x$ to $y$ and from $x$ to $z$ form a positive basis, and then move it parallel to itself until it passes through the origin. The result is an element $G(x,y,z)$ of the Grassmann manifold $\mathrm{G}_2\mathbb R^4$ of all oriented 2-planes through the origin

blocks.content: []{#sec:top_proof label="sec:top_proof"} Starting with a link in the $3$-sphere, consider the ***delta move*** shown in Figure [1](#fig:delta){reference-type="ref" reference="fig:delta"}, which may be thought of as a higher order variant of a crossing change. Sketch of the proof of Theorem ??
blocks.content: []{#sec:thmB label="sec:thmB"} Let $L$ be a 3-component link in $S^3$ with pairwise linking numbers $p$, $q$ and $r$ all zero. We saw in Theorem [\[thm:A\]](#thm:A){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:A"} that these numbers are the degrees of the characteristic map $g_L: T^3 \to S^2$ on the 2-dimensional coordinate subtori. Thus $g_L$ is homotopic to a map which collapses the 2-skeleton of $T^3$, and so is in effect a map of $S^3 \to S^2$.
